description:
## 2.0.1

- feat: add Cancel, rename Done to Save — autosave keeps dismissal
- feat: hotkey editor autosaves — dismiss-anything commits

patches.name: Bypass Gboard Signature
patches.description: Bypass Gboard's signature whitelist checks and force them to pass.

patches.name: Grammar Check Row
patches.description: Force the grammar check settings row to appear. The Phenotype flag that governs it never syncs on a patched build, so its compiled-in default (off) sticks.

patches.name: Install as Gboard Clone
patches.description: Rename the package to dev.jz6.com.google.android.inputmethod.latin so the patched build installs alongside the official Gboard instead of replacing it.

patches.name: Suggested Settings
patches.description: Turns on flick keys for symbols, touch & hold keys for numbers, suggestion strip, grammar check and smart replies, and turns off block offensive words and word suggestions. Written once as defaults, so each can still be changed in Gboard's own settings.

patches.name: Swipe Right to Undo
patches.description: Swipe right after deleting to put the words back. Uses Gboard's own undo, which already records what a delete swipe removed.

patches.name: Swipe to Delete
patches.description: Swipe left anywhere on the keyboard to delete the previous word, and swipe right to restore it. Uses Gboard's own word-scrub engine, so it behaves exactly like swiping on the backspace key already does — only it can start anywhere.

patches.name: Toolbar Buttons
patches.description: Add Select all, Copy and Paste buttons to the toolbar above the keyboard, so each is one tap instead of opening Gboard's text editing panel first. Registered natively, so drag-to-reorder through the toolbar customize page persists.

patches.name: Toolbar Hotkeys
patches.description: Adds six configurable hotkey slots to Gboard's toolbar — each commits a text of your choice on tap. A slot appears when its text is set; when cleared it hides at the next toolbar rebuild (rotate, switch IME, or restart — there's no mid-session un-register). Text and icon edits apply on the next keyboard open.

patches.name: Toolbar Native Test
patches.description: Add a 'Test' button to the toolbar through Gboard's own access-point registry so drag reorder and persistence work natively. Writes 'test' at the cursor on tap. Architectural proof-of-concept; off by default.

release_notes:
## 2.4.2

- fix: a flag scan that failed on another bundle's merged extension
- docs: draft option B against the dex, and verify the claim it rests on
- docs: read out the handler registry's consumer, and reverse the recommendation
- docs: Gboard does not instantiate motion event handlers by reflection
- fix: act on an independent review of the four unpushed commits
- refactor: the resolution helpers take a class lookup, not the patcher
- test: cover the register helpers, which is where the crashes came from
- test: lock in the mutual exclusion, and ask whether the bundle is current
- fix: the driver applied a combination no install can produce
- test: cover the patch helpers, document the output tools, assert the Python floor
- ci: catch drift in the generated inventory and README table
- feat: check extension references, and admit the general case needs the SDK
- test: run the extension's logic, not just compile it
- feat: verify invoke arguments and catch-handler merges
- docs: correct development.md, which was three beliefs out of date
- feat: verify every method the patch changed, automatically
- ci: upload the bundle on every push, so a patch can be tested before it ships
- feat: a type-merge check for the bug ART rejects at class load
- docs: what the driver covers, and what it does not
- feat: run the patches locally — :driver:run was never blocked
- docs: the dev.1 crash, diagnosed by reading the output
- feat: read the patched APK, not just the stock one
- docs: improve the replan — the cause is unknown and the tooling is the gap
- docs: replan swipe up to undo autocorrect
- revert: drop the consume branch, it ships a keyboard that will not open
- fix: the consume branch shipped a keyboard that would not open
- fix: swipe up consumes the gesture and lowers the slide threshold
